result.evidence: All four refutations fail against the complete bundled artifact. (a) Present under another name: the canonical command inventory at line 63, nested canonical/bootstrap specs (lines 112–185), and full task tree specify completion, evidence recovery and no-effect attempt closure, but no terminal disposition for a confirmed creation that cannot finish. BootstrapStatus only recovers existing evidence (line 71); completed cleanup only applies after downstream completion (line 75); --not-created closes an uncertain attempt as no-effect and authorizes another attempt (line 81), not the whole bootstrap. (b) Within the stated contract: missing-pane refusal and nonexpiring protection are intentional safety rules (lines 67,73), but they do not expressly accept permanent archival veto after abandonment. The accepted limit at line 83 sacrifices automatic progress across response loss and permits explicit inspection recovery; it does not cover truthfully ending a confirmed, subsequently unusable creation. A manual terminal disposition could preserve both refusal to relocate and honest creation evidence without weakening these rules. (c) Out of scope: this concerns the explicitly included bootstrap lifecycle and archival integration, not automatic tab cleanup, recreation, identity transfer or stronger distributed guarantees. Line 85 forbids automatic closure of created tabs; releasing an abandoned workflow's protection need not close any topology. (d) Immaterial: begin against an existing thread installs protection before creation (line 67). Take the exact missing-pane state expressly covered by line 73 after successful creation is recorded but before attachment/downstream completion. Retry cannot resolve/attach that topology; completion cannot pass line 75; --created-pane cannot obtain coherent current evidence for the missing result and --not-created cannot truthfully assert noncreation (line 81). The existing thread's veto therefore remains live (lines 67,89), even after deleting local progress or retiring the seat. This permanently prevents archival of an otherwise finished existing thread, making the missing terminal path significant. Should-fix: successful handoffs remain viable, but the irreversible lifecycle blockage requires a defined operator disposition. This is an internal state-machine finding; no external API premise is needed.
